Subject: Seneca x Redwood - updated commercial proposal (3yr)

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement and Finance at Seneca have reviewed the term sheet and have two main asks before they can route to the CFO for sign-off: a firm cap on annual price increases and a renewal protection that limits surprise uplifts at the end of the term. Attached is the updated forecast and the redlines we started in track changes.

High level: 3-year term, committed baseline 8M tokens/month, option to scale quarterly. They are asking for: 
- annual uplift cap <= 6% (they are proposing 5% but want to see if Redwood will accept 6% max),
- price collar that prevents >10% downside (i.e., they want a minimum effective floor if usage falls),
- renewal protection clause: if market rates increase >12% at renewal, Redwood would provide a one-time credit to offset the delta (amount TBD),
- DocuSign-ready contract — they prefer a single-signature flow.

Can you confirm whether these three items are acceptable from a deal desk standpoint? Marcus is copying in case he needs any additional financials.

Best,
Aisha
Procurement Manager 
Seneca Therapeutics

Attachments: Seneca_MA-Usage_Forecast.xlsx (xlsx), SEN-DA-Redlines-v3.pdf (pdf)

From: nikhil_sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Seneca x Redwood - updated commercial proposal (3yr) — need exec signoff guidance

Marissa, Lauren — forwarding Seneca's asks. Quick summary and recommendation below.

Summary of customer asks:
- 3-year term with baseline commit 8M tokens/mo
- annual uplift cap requested 6% (they suggested 5%)
- price collar / floor to limit downside exposure when usage drops
- renewal protection: credit if market >12% at renewal

Recommended approach (Deal Desk draft):
1) Approve 3-year term with baseline commit and quarterly scale metrics.
2) Accept an annual uplift cap of 6% BUT gate it to: (a) a minimum annualized revenue threshold (to prevent compounding creep), and (b) re-evaluate after year 2 if we see consistent under-utilization.
3) Price collar: counter-propose an indexed floor (effective floor not lower than 85% of current price) rather than an absolute % floor. This protects revenue but keeps flexibility.
4) Renewal protection: offer a one-time renewal credit equal to 50% of the delta between Redwood list and market increase, capped at 3% of the ARR. This preserves commercial protection but limits Redwood exposure.

Attached is an exec approval template with the precise ask we should present for signoff (exec_approval_template.docx). If you both approve, I'll pull legal to accept the redlines and then route to CEO / CFO for signoff.

Notes: Seneca is strategic — they plan to embed Redwood across three product lines next year. We should weigh upside against this limited term exposure.

-Nikhil
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: exec_approval_template.docx (docx)

Thanks Nikhil — I agree with the recommended approach with small edits:

Edits to propose to execs:
- Annual uplift cap: mark as 6% but with an explicit provision that any uplift above 4% in a single year requires a customer notice and 90-day right to terminate without penalty. This protects us operationally.
- Price collar: prefer fixed floor at 80% of current effective rate (simpler to explain to finance).
- Renewal credit: 50% of delta capped at 2% of ARR (reduce Redwood liability slightly).

If legal is comfortable with the floor language, I'm prepared to route for executive review. Recommend we show modeled P&L for downside scenarios (attached quick tab in the forecast).

-Lauren
VP, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
